newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Little inflation seen in PPI.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Little inflation seen in PPI.

text.p: U.S. producer prices (PPI) will occupy bond market participants' attention on Wednesday following little reaction to as-expected retail sales data on Tuesday.

Bond market prices were little moved on Tuesday by April retail sales data, which showed the expected decline of 0.3 percent. Economists polled by Reuters expected that producer prices would remain unchanged in April, but rise 0.1 percent excluding the volatile food and energy components -- still tame numbers suggesting little inflation.
PPI will be followed on Thursday by the consumer price index, figures William Griggs, managing director at Griggs & Santow Inc, said would be bond market friendly.
"I don't know (producer prices) will help the market as the market already expects it to be good," Griggs said. "But we're looking for second quarter growth to come off quite a bit."
Griggs said growth, while slowing, was still above the trend the Fed would like to see. That would push the central bank to tighten by another 25 basis points at its next meeting on May 20, he said.
Griggs said the Federal Reserve likely would move to tighten monetary policy sooner rather than later, instead of stringing out its movements.
"We're looking for a tame PPI. The market was reacting today to some rumors of the Fed moving," said Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc.

Reuters reported earlier in the session that sources close to the Fed expected the central bank to tighten short-term interest rates by 25 basis points. It last moved to ratchet rates up at its meeting on March 25.
Kretzmer said even weak retail sales, PPI and CPI may not be enough to stop the Fed from moving.

"Clearly the market is more nervous that they will move anyway," Kretzmer said. Despite that, he said there was plenty of reason for the Fed to wait -- that the economy was slowing in the second half.
"It's a skewed type of bet tomorrow. Good intermediate and core numbers, the market improves. But bad PPI, the markets will come off," Kretzmer said.
He said he did not think it was necessary for the Fed to tighten interest rates at its meeting next week.
In late trading Tuesday the 30-year bond was off 14/32 at 96-08/32 to yield 6.92 percent.
At the short end the three-month bill was down two basis points at 5.07 percent. The six-month was up one basis point at 5.33 percent and the year bill was up four basis points at 5.55 percent.
Ten-year notes were down 12/32 at 99-12/32 to yield 6.71 percent. Five-year issues were down 8/32 at 100-08 to yield 6.56 percent and two-years were off 4/32 at 100-05/32 to yield 6.29 percent.
